title: I Posted the Ice-Cream Sample Limit After They Scooped a Flight for Staff

parts.text: I asked for the posted two-sample limit at 3:18 p.m. and scoop lead Tess was already plating a six-taste flight into a STAFF ONLY boat. The case card said: TWO TASTES. THEN BUY. NO STAFF FLIGHTS ON THE CLOCK. I was twenty-two, customer, holding a kid who had been told one. Tess winked. "Staff are the case." I photographed the boat, the card, and the kid's empty spoon. Then I logged a flight. At 3:24 the owner asked why Tess's boat was on a sample-limit ticket. I did not argue the joke. I argued the file. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The owner can see Tess's staff boat on a six-taste flight against the two-taste card.

social.video_title: She plated a staff flight under a two-taste card — Part 1/2
social.description: Ice cream, a kid's spoon, and a case card the lead posted. I logged the flight. Would you have photographed the boat?

parts.text: Tess called it training until the owner asked for the ticket. I printed the flight, the photo, and the card. The boat went back. Tess tasted two like the kid and told the line training was always about optics. Optics is a word scoops use when a boat exists. Sample policy now has a second line: STAFF ARE NOT THE CASE. I keep two spoons. Tess brown-bags. The shop finally looks like a case, not a back room. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point. If it is written, it can be applied to the person who wrote it.

social.video_title: Staff are not the case — Part 2/2
social.description: Flight ticket, returned boat, and a second line. Was training ever six tastes?
